reviews.body: Restricted view tickets should not be sold (or bought) as this really means you cannot see the stage at all. So very disappointing as the music was brilliant. As we couldn’t see the stage couldn’t say whether the acting or lighting was good but as the music was so good can only say the acting probably matched the music.

reviews.title: A bright uplifting evening amidst the cold, dark, winter post Christmas January days - but good fun entertainmet anytime
reviews.author: Manina

reviews.author: Ilaria

reviews.title: Very entertaining 👏
reviews.body: Good music, great acting, catchy tunes. Good lighting.
reviews.author: Ruth

reviews.title: A good show
reviews.body: I liked the show, unfortunately didn’t love it. There was nothing wrong with the performance in general (loved Allie Daniel as Hermes!) and I honestly don’t think I could explain why, but it just fell a bit flat to me. It didn’t transport me like other musicals did.
reviews.author: Selma

reviews.title: Magnificent show
reviews.body: Brilliant from start to finish - we are definitely coming again

reviews.title: Good show seats are for small people

reviews.title: Stupendous!

reviews.author: Lesley

reviews.title: Interesting Night at the Theatre
reviews.body: It has a style of its own, wouldn't see it twice but I was entertained. Sat in the gods so it didn't cost much either (£35 per ticket isn't bad for a West End theatre)
reviews.author: Nicholas

reviews.title: The most amazing show of the season!
reviews.body: Absolutely stunning interpretation of Greek legend, amazing jazz music, vivid characters, clever script. Must be seen by every thinking human of any age. Lots of joy!

reviews.title: Wonderful evening with a fabulous performance all round

reviews.title: Great understudy performances and main cast!!

reviews.author: M.p.e.

reviews.title: ONE OF THE BEST SHOWS I'VE EVER SEEN
reviews.body: I cannot praise this production enough. It is so original - uplifting, sad, poignant, moving, gripping, surprising, all at the same time! Dazzling. Wonderful performances by the actors, catchy tunes, great costumes, choreography exceptional... I really can't praise it enough!
reviews.author: Santa

reviews.title: Amazing story told in such a beautifully tragic way!
reviews.author: Corey

reviews.title: Nothing memorable
reviews.body: Nothing memorable about this show. This is certainly NOT the best show in town. Just go two doors along to the Guilgud and see Oliver! The cast worked hard though.
reviews.author: Kenneth

reviews.title: Loved all of it - the music, the singers, the dancers, it was wonderful!
reviews.author: Chloe

reviews.title: Fabulous upbeat musical
reviews.body: Loved it
reviews.author: Aleta

reviews.title: Stunningly beautiful and moving
reviews.body: The experience was incredible. The cast intertwined beautifully with the band, and filling up that stage with intricate vocals and deep emotion. A delicious treat! We laughed, we cried, we lived. Thank you to the whole team for a wonderful evening!!!
reviews.author: Ines

reviews.title: A different musical
reviews.body: Great cast, recommended for those who love musicals with a lot of singing and little dancing
reviews.author: Roberto

reviews.title: Got completely carried away
reviews.body: I only knew the story but i got carried away by the actors and the singing. More emotional than i thought it would be. Strong use of the podium and ome really talented people.
reviews.author: Glenn

reviews.title: Amazing trip down below!
reviews.body: Cast and crew were excellent. We enjoyed every second of this amazing story. Can't wait to be back.
reviews.author: Stefanie

reviews.title: Stunning, powerful and beautiful
reviews.body: Absolutely adored this show. I was on the edge of my seat and so were the rest of the audience. The music, singing and acting were powerful and moving. So many amazing melodies. Loved the casting. The young people I was with loved it as much as me.
reviews.author: Heather

reviews.title: Masterfully done!
reviews.body: This is one musical i had the opportunity watching at Lyrics Theater is a breath of fresh air! Conventional Classic plays are great by the way … dont get me wrong. Hadestown however “ROCKS”! Glad i watched it with my daughter night before leaving London!
reviews.author: Neilson

reviews.title: Fun, meaningful, great music
reviews.body: The performers were excellent and the story prompted discussion for several days.
reviews.author: Sarah

reviews.title: Spectacular cult musical
reviews.body: Being of retirement age my group were the oldest to attend this production. There was a lot of whooping and clapping throughout, at times masking the performance. If you like Jazz and dance then this can overcome the storyline which is told through song and music which was hard to hear individual words at times. Overall a great performance but not for everyone.
reviews.author: Denise

reviews.title: absolutely spectacular
reviews.body: A masterclass in music, acting, lyrics and choreography, hadestown was incredible
reviews.author: Claire

reviews.title: Exceptional
reviews.body: Refreshing, engaging, captivating even. Plus a very well deserved long standing ovation!
reviews.author: Francis

reviews.title: Brilliant and emotive!
reviews.body: I loved the show, the acting, music and musicians, and general vibe was immaculate. Orpheus, Eurydice, Hades and Persephone were especially amazing, (Waylon Jacobs as Hades was absolutely epic give him the role pls!!) but everyone was absolutely stunning. The trombone player stood out to me too, his playing was stellar. Overall loved it, and would definitely come back.
reviews.author: Nancy

reviews.title: Must watch.
reviews.body: This is a great show. The music is fantastic and so is the acting. Fabulous telling of a great Greek myth.
reviews.author: Rowena

reviews.title: Progressive music
reviews.body: Modern combination of jazz, folk, blues R&B. Good songs and singing, movement and acting. Excellent support musicians (especially drummer and trombone. I was amazed to see such a young, enthusiastic audience. Some around me indicated that they had heard the CD or seen the show before. A great night out.
reviews.author: Ga

reviews.title: One the best musicals in town!
reviews.body: The musical touches in human nature themes in a beautiful, educational and entertaining way! I had great conversations with my kids about the flaws of human nature and what drives them. Great night!!
reviews.author: Cristina

reviews.title: Enjoyable romp, jazz fused musical
reviews.body: Vibrant show with enthusiastic actors and but the score was un memorable bar three songs. may be being a bit harsh but once in Hades would have expected the score to turn menacing and a bit dark but maintained the pace and mood of the first act. Musicianship excellent.
reviews.author: James

reviews.title: Not sure about this

reviews.title: An Oldenburg Story to be seen.

reviews.title: Exceptional Experience

reviews.author: Denise

reviews.title: A show that is not to be missed!

reviews.title: Excellent and Entertaining Production

reviews.author: Garry

reviews.title: Excellent production, but Lyric needs a makeover…
reviews.body: Great performances and fantastic staging, offset by Lyric’s underlying odour and a ventilation system so loud that it invades the quieter moments, often making the more subtle dialogue near impossible to hear
reviews.author: Andrew

reviews.title: Great show!
reviews.body: Lovely music with themes relevant to today’s world events.
reviews.author: Chloé

reviews.title: An Australian Perspective
reviews.body: Hadestown is the finest example of what can be accomplished in musical theatre. It is exhilarating in every respect. I attend a show each time I visit London and this is one reinforces that commitment. Do see it if you possibly can.
reviews.author: Alan Robin

reviews.title: Great show!

reviews.title: Aaamazing show

reviews.author: Paula

reviews.title: Foot tappingly good

reviews.author: Sarah

reviews.title: Hadestown

reviews.title: Vibrant
reviews.body: Fabto experience
reviews.author: Claire

reviews.title: A musical spectacular
reviews.body: This is a great show with a great story line and some really catchy songs. The sound was not perfect as I couldn’t understand all the lyrics (or maybe some of the actors need to work on their delivery).
reviews.author: Alistair

reviews.title: A gorgeous soundscape and feast for the eyes
reviews.body: I absolutely loved this show. The music is gorgeous varying from New Orleans style jazz to emo ballads. The singers were fantastic and the lighting and set were stunning.
reviews.author: David

reviews.title: Interesting concept
reviews.body: This is a high energy show, beautifully performed by the actors and dancers. The set is great and visually stunning. My criticism is that the story rambles at times and is difficult to hear the words as the balance between music and voice is wrong. I struggled to hear what Hermes was saying, despite her vibrant performance.
reviews.author: Ann

reviews.title: Hadestown is an emotional trip through the underworld and gods from the past .
reviews.body: Excellent acting and singing . I only cried three times through the performance and that is because I had to control myself . It was an emotional, evocative and thoughtful performance. Excellent cast , staging , and music . Great story makes this show a joy to go to live theatre .
reviews.author: Dana

reviews.title: Unexpectedly wonderful
reviews.body: I didnt know what I was going in to but this show was an unexpectedly wonderful experience. Everything from the cast and the music to the stageart and lighting.
reviews.author: Lisa

reviews.title: Beautiful show, heartfelt story, and wonderful music
reviews.author: Lucy

reviews.title: Unique musical theatre experience
reviews.body: Hades town brought Greek myths bang up to date and into a New Orleans jazz cafe! The musicianship was phenomenal and the acting and performing were world class too. It totally draws you into the story with some incredible songs, great messages about modern society and brilliant use of stage management with the revolving stage and trapdoor. Funny, moving, thought-provoking and a must-see!
reviews.author: Tim

reviews.title: A pleasant, lively, easy to watch show
reviews.body: I personally found the first half a bit slow but found the second half much better - without spoiling the story, the ending could have been a bit more upbeat.
reviews.author: Mark

reviews.title: A must see!
reviews.body: Hadestown is brilliant, and the actors- every single one of them- are electric!

reviews.title: See it while Mason Alexander Park is still playing Mary
reviews.body: The show is hilarious and irreverent. And - with all due respect to Cole Escola - no one is a better Mary than Mason Alexander Park. That b***h is turned up to 11. Their performance could only be better if those other actors would just get out of the way! A magnificent f***ing c**t!
reviews.author: Jonathan

reviews.body: If you like a farce it’s farcical. A packed theatre and half a dozen people laughed like it was the funniest thing they had ever seen. The rest of us waited 35 mins for a funny gag. The last 20 mins was very good musically and plot wise but the first hour was poor. Not funny but it thought it was.
reviews.author: Christopher

reviews.title: OMG
reviews.body: It is one of the best show I have ever seen. The cast is fantastic and the plot is very funny. Highly and strong recommended
reviews.author: Manuela

reviews.title: Comedy in its highest level
reviews.body: Fantastic show , inventive , wacky , crazy, perfectly timed ..and the cast a 10, and him/her mind blowing!!!!

reviews.title: Extraordinary! But excellent.
reviews.body: Very amusing, disrespectful, rude, satirical postmodern show with a strong gay (etc) slant.
reviews.author: P.a

reviews.title: Wacky, fun and funny
reviews.body: I am an American and a true fan of Abraham Lincoln. I had no idea what the show was about, and after the first few moments of shock, I settled in and realized that this was one of the funniest, wackiest show's I've seen. I would see it again!!!!
reviews.author: Jill

reviews.title: Weird and wonderful - excellent acting
reviews.body: This was a weird surreal and highly entertaining show….. with lots of farcical elements. Not quite sure how I would explain the story other than to say the writer has a wild imagination. All actors were great but the lead was amazing - hysterical.
reviews.author: Reilly

reviews.title: The real story of Abe&Co
reviews.body: Don’t ask anyone who’s seen the show what it’s all about. From the start, surprises, outrageous skits and breathtaking athleticism are blended - and only those of Trumpian demeanour might keep a straight face. Rollicking good fun, sharp lines and momentum till the final curtain.
reviews.author: John

reviews.title: Worst show I have ever seen.
reviews.body: It relies on worn out stereotypes of women, mental illness, and LGBQ+ people. It ridicules them. Setting it in the White House and using Abraham Lincoln and Mary Todd Lincoln as characters, is a cheap trick and offense. The disclaimers do not mitigate the offense.
reviews.author: Kenneth

reviews.title: Funny
reviews.body: Funny show, very camp and quite rude. Not the sort of show i normally book but was recommended. I like music and singing so I loved the cabaret ending! Glad I went and would recommend.
reviews.author: Tracy

reviews.title: Surprisingly Very Funny
reviews.body: This show was amazingly clever, amusing, funny, well-acted. So good!
reviews.author: Anne

reviews.title: Elusive seating plan
reviews.body: Not sure I I found the seating plan , but I did by chance , maybe more to do with my difficulty with i phone technology .

reviews.title: Good service

reviews.title: It is over a decade I use London Box Office UK! Strongly recommended
reviews.body: Yes I always use it to find very cheap tickets for amazing shows
Very accessible website and easy to make bookongs

reviews.title: Not for me
reviews.body: Learnt more about American independence. The teenagers in the audience seemed to enjoy it but I found the words difficult to hear and didn’t care for the sexualisation of the female dancers especially because they would not have dressed like that in this period. The cast need to be told that there is a paying audience above the stalls. They neve4 looked up.
reviews.author: Janet

reviews.title: Banger!
reviews.body: I have not seen Hamilton before so it was a bit hard to follow the story. Otherwise the best show I’ve ever been to. Scenography and choreography was incredible! And amazing actors & dancers!
reviews.author: Iris

reviews.title: Absolutely brilliant! Loved the story, the music, the pace and the casting was great!

reviews.title: Absolutely incredible

reviews.title: All the humour, warmth and emotion of the best stories
reviews.body: This show has me laughing, thinking, crying, and being thoroughly entertained. The details of the performance in the dance, the lighting, the set - it's just brilliant. Still the standout shown at the West End at the moment
reviews.author: Irene

reviews.title: Incredible
reviews.body: Amazing on every level. Talent, creativity, skill, story telling, dancing and a privilege to be immersed in such incredible singing.
reviews.author: Suzanne

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.body: The best musical I have seen. Brilliant cast, beautiful theatre, gripping story line and wide variety of genre of music.
reviews.author: Karen

reviews.title: Excellent show!
reviews.body: This show is amazing!! Everything was brilliant!! One word of advice, if you don’t know the story, I would research it before watching as some of the rapping especially in the first half of the first part is so fast it’s hard to follow!! But the rapping is so lyrical and clever, keep your ears peeled!!
reviews.author: Rita

reviews.title: Very creative and a must see
reviews.body: From the beginning before the stage set draws you in. The singing was excellent whether it was a soloist or harmonies it was excellent. The choreography again was very creative excellently executed by the performers. I cannot fault this show.My partner and I loved it and will commend it to everyone.
reviews.author: Everts

reviews.title: AMAZING
reviews.body: This show was gripping from start to finish singing, dancing all amazing would definitely see again
reviews.author: Jenna

reviews.title: Amazing show
reviews.body: The show from start to finish was just the best, the music and singing was at times quite emotional, the story was easy to follow, even for those who maybe didn’t previously know the story of Hamilton. I can see myself coming for a repeat performance, and I’ve never thought that of any other production I’ve seen.
reviews.author: Paula

reviews.body: Theatre not good, went with children,used Theatre booster seats, they told by Theatre staff they couldn't used them after people behind complain. Yet they handed out some booster cushions to some adult ladies. You pay a lot of money for the tickets, and even us as adults had a problem to see. So even though the show and actors are amazing. I wouldn't recommend going,
reviews.author: Carol

reviews.title: Choreography and musicality show must to be seen
reviews.author: Maureen Ann

reviews.title: Very Disappointing
reviews.body: I left this performance just after half time. The ‘music’ is poor and melodies very repetitious. The sounds are boring. The dancing prancing around the stsge is pointless. It is difficult to capture a historical story in a musical. However the ‘rap’ genre did nothing to help this. A very overrated show. We were ber disappointed. Lovely theatre and our seating gave us a near perfect view of the stage. Leg room a little cramped.
reviews.author: Terence

reviews.title: Epic, historical story and fantastic costumes
reviews.body: Didn't know too much about the Hamilton story but it was easy to follow and it was an epic show with great costumes and great acting...loved the King and admittedly we did cry at the end!
reviews.author: Debra

reviews.body: The theatre was too hot- air conditioning required as it got uncomfortable
reviews.author: Nisha

reviews.title: So different from all the productions I’ve seen
reviews.author: Sheena

reviews.title: Amazing show
reviews.body: I came with 2 friends, none of us had any expectations though we'd all heard 'it's great'. We all left talking about the performance, story, songs, everything we loved it.
reviews.author: Samantha

reviews.title: Definitely a must see
reviews.body: Was a fantastic show was so good had everyone laughing at times was so much fun
reviews.author: Lisa

reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.body: I have been meaning to go for years and had high hopes. You don’t pay so much for a ticket if you don’t. I enjoyed the performances from the start but often leave at the interval. I was very engaged 20 mins in and it got even better from there. Didn’t musicals used to have happy stories? Had my handkerchief in my hand for the last 30. Fabulous cast, fabulous show. Thank you!
reviews.author: Nicholas

reviews.title: 5th time and just as good
reviews.body: What I love about seeing Hamilton again for the fifth time in the last decade is that the show still has layers you haven’t seen before no matter how well you know it? Each time you see a new cast you find and see something different in the interpretation - well done to the current London West End cast - you are absolutely holding your own against the previous greats!
reviews.author: Sarah

reviews.title: Fabulous
reviews.body: Great show, great songs
reviews.author: Linda

reviews.title: Simply fantastic
reviews.body: By far the best show I have seen for years - possibly ever. I look forward to see it again shortly.
reviews.author: Jesper

reviews.title: High Energy, Fun and Educationalperformance
reviews.body: It’s not what I expected but absolutely loved it, a really modern take on American History. Take your teenagers they will love it!

reviews.title: Brilliant show
reviews.body: We came all the way from the Netherlands and we found it a great show special recommendestions for Jefferson we loved every minute

reviews.body: Excellent show music great

reviews.title: Very good story, music and dancing
reviews.author: Sean

reviews.title: Powerful, a must see!

reviews.author: Harneen

reviews.title: Great show
reviews.body: Really good show however sometimes the volume of the music overpowered the voices.
reviews.author: Christine

reviews.title: Absolutely jaw dropping

reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: Outstanding Performance we was blown away amazing singers fantastic.
reviews.body: We was blown away with actors and the singing was amazing from start to finish.. fantastic performance and this is an all round show teenagers would love this also it’s one all bring all together.

reviews.body: Please read the history before going to the show

reviews.title: The storyline covers a vast amount that takes you through multiple emotions. It’s put together with such good structure and easy to follow. The actors are all amazing singer and dancers. I love how each character had a moment in the like light to show mor

reviews.body: The show was a lot of fun. Great sings, great singing. But I recommend you do your homework on Alexander Hamilton before you go, or you won't have a clue what's going on.

reviews.title: Superb storytelling
reviews.body: First visit to Victoria Palace. Staff are helpful. I read up about American history beforehand which helped as the performance goes at a fast pace.
reviews.author: Paul

reviews.title: Great music & rapping
reviews.body: Booked on a recommendation and was great. Would go & see it again!
reviews.author: Cheryl

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.body: Unfortunately had a tech problem in second half,but the end was worth waiting for
reviews.author: Alison

reviews.title: Second time
reviews.body: Saw Rufus production in 2018. Still fresh still important piece of history told through music and spoken word poetry. The actors were uniformly good but a special call out to King George and Jefferson who were memorable. The sound system was a bit of a challenge- percussion often too loud and a few actors often needed stronger mics. But these a small quibbles.
reviews.author: Margaret

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.body: Really good worth seeing
reviews.author: Ian

reviews.title: The cost has now come down to reasonable after years of waiting
reviews.body: Fantastic show have waited years to see it as cost was exorbitant

reviews.body: Very entertaining didn’t know story and unclear fir first half hour but in the end fantastic performance

reviews.title: Definitely a must see!
reviews.body: I had a fantastic time seeing The Devil Wears Prada at the Dominion Theatre. I traveled to London specifically to see the show before Vanessa Williams finishes her run next month, and it absolutely lived up to the trip. The entire production is beautifully done. The cast is outstanding across the board, with excellent acting, singing, and dancing that keeps the energy high from start to finish. Vanessa Williams is perfectly cast and commands the stage with the exact presence you’d expect from Miranda Priestly. The rest of the ensemble is equally strong and brings great chemistry and humor to the story. The set design and staging are especially impressive. Scene changes are smooth and visually striking, and the production makes great use of the theatre space to create a glamorous, fast-moving world that fits the story perfectly. Overall, it’s a polished, entertaining production that captures the spirit and wit of the original film while feeling fresh as a live musical. I went with a friend who lives in London, and we both had an excellent evening. If you’re a fan of the movie or just enjoy a stylish, high-energy musical, this show is absolutely worth seeing.

reviews.title: Lovely to Look At, But Lacking Real Spark
reviews.body: I really wanted to love My Neighbour Totoro but in the end I found it more average than magical. It moved quite slowly, and while I understand that having adults play very young children is unavoidable, I found it a little off-putting and it sometimes made it harder to stay immersed in the story. There were certainly lovely moments, seeing Totoro and the other characters brought to life on stage was genuinely wonderful. But once that initial moment of magic passed it didn’t quite sustain the same sense of wonder for the whole performance. Overall it felt like there wasn’t quite enough of any one element: not quite enough fun, love, pathos or music to fully carry it. That said, the sets were excellent, crafted with great care and well used which added a lot visually to the production.

reviews.title: A Truly Special Night at My Neighbour Totoro
reviews.body: I went to see My Neighbour Totoro at the Gillian Lynne Theatre in the West End having never watched the film before, so I wasn’t sure what to expect. From the moment I arrived, the experience was wonderful. The theatre was clean, the seats were comfortable, and the staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming. The theatre is also perfectly located, just five minutes from Holborn station and a short walk from a great selection of lovely restaurants, which made it easy to enjoy a meal before the show and turn the evening into a real treat. The show itself was magical and felt like a true reconnection with my inner child and imagination. The band and singer brought the production to life beautifully and added so much emotion to the performance. Afterwards, I watched the animated film and realised just how incredible a job the stage production had done in bringing the animation to life. It is not just for families either. Adults looking for something a little different will enjoy it just as much. A truly special theatre experience that I would happily recommend.

From unwillingness to let waiting spectators inside the line dividers or inside the salon to stopping the performers from finishing their songs (was someone in production asked to start clapping hands just to be able to cut it short?) All the way to the end when the curtain fell and the cheers were hushed and the NO RECORDING was pointed out. (Why even do this when the performers are receiving the final cheers?) reviews.title: The Book of Mormon Loves Musicals More Than You!
reviews.body: As everyone with a modicum of intelligence knows, musicals are the highest form of art. Nowhere is this more gleefully affirmed than in The Book of Mormon, Trey Parker, Matt Stone, and Robert Lopez’s audacious Broadway juggernaut. On the surface, it’s exactly what you might expect from the minds behind South Park: irreverent, blasphemous, and more than a little crude. Yet beneath the outrageous gags and taboo-poking humour lies a deeply affectionate celebration of the musical as an art form. What makes The Book of Mormon remarkable is how fully it embraces, and even worships, the classic structures of musical theatre. Its opening number, “Hello,” is a pitch-perfect parody of the “welcome to our world” trope, while songs like “You and Me (But Mostly Me)” and “Turn It Off” directly echo Broadway traditions, from bombastic hero duets to tap-dancing showstoppers. Every number, no matter how shocking the lyrics, is staged with a knowing wink to the lineage of Rodgers and Hammerstein, Stephen Sondheim, and even Disney. The satire may cut deep, but it is built on reverence. The crude jokes, then, aren’t ends in themselves but tools to remind us of the enduring optimism and transformative power of the genre. Even when the story veers into absurdity, the characters remain grounded in that classic musical tradition: dreamers who believe, against all odds, that song and faith (whether in God, in friendship, or in storytelling itself) can change the world. In its final moments, when the missionaries find new meaning through myth-making, the show slyly suggests that belief and theatre share the same DNA: both demand a suspension of disbelief, and both, at their best, can give people hope. Far from mocking the genre, The Book of Mormon exalts it. Its irreverence is a disguise for devotion, its vulgarity a counterpoint that makes its earnestness shine all the brighter. This is not just a comedy about religion, it is a love letter to musicals themselves, reminding us that no matter how cynical the world becomes, there is nothing quite as subversively powerful as a chorus line singing in perfect harmony

reviews.title: You don’t need roads!
reviews.body: A treat for husband’s 67th birthday, a fan of the original film when it was first released. Our adult son came too, having been introduced to the film as a teenager. The musical certainly delivered with the DeLorean spectacle. We were trying to figure how the elevation above the audience was achieved! Likewise the clever effect of Doc at the clock in the storm was impressive. The whole cast were full of energy and maintained that throughout. Shoutout to the dancers who had so many costume and character changes. Doc played up to the audience hilariously. The second half was the best. Some of the musical numbers in the first half were padded out too much (almost as much as Lorraine’s bra!). Would have preferred more dialogue between Marty and Doc. Mr McFly’s peeping Tom song was cringy ( no reflection on the actor, who gave it his all during all his scenes. Overall, a great celebration of Back to the Future, particularly for original fans of the film, making it feel fresh and fantastical once once.

reviews.title: Very disappointed.
reviews.body: I waited a long time to see this show. Love the films so this was a no brainier, however i felt like walking out during the interval but was persuaded to stay by those i was with. Follows the general storyline with lines from the film, but then there’s completely random nonsense like Marty whipping out a lightsaber. A lot of scenes that were added to the stage adaptation were just confusing and nonsensical. Also probably 90% of the songs were ‘crowbarred’ in and had no relevance to the story, it’s like they wrote a copy of the film for stage then decided to make it a musical and hastily shoehorned a load of songs in random places without really caring if it fits the current part of the story. I see 6/7 shows a year and this has to be up there with the worst i’ve seen in years. I was praying for it to end about 10 mins into the second half. At £105 per ticket i feel well and truly ripped off. The actors playing Doc and Marty seems to have forgotten their lines on several occasions and were waiting to be fed them- long awkward pauses between lines made me cringe. And also another detail was the lack of attention to detail was evident- as Marty is well known for wearing Nike training shoes in the film but the actor on stage wasn’t. If you can’t even be bothered to get iconic details correct, might as well give up. I’m surprised they had a DeLorean as the car and didn’t just substitute it with a Ford Sierra hoping no one would notice! The script when it diverted from the film was poor too- , with several people around me groaning at the poor attempt at humour. Honestly- don’t bother- there are so many more much better films to spend your money on.

reviews.title: Absolutely fantastic show
reviews.body: Short Theatre Review – Back to the Future: The Musical Back to the Future: The Musical is a thrilling, high-energy stage adaptation that brings the beloved story to life with spectacular effects, catchy songs, and plenty of humor. The performances are lively and engaging, capturing the charm and excitement of Marty and Doc’s time-travel adventure. The standout feature is the incredible staging—especially the DeLorean scenes—which create real theatrical magic and keep the audience fully immersed. With its mix of nostalgia, heart, and fun, the show is an entertaining experience for both longtime fans and newcomers. Verdict: A fast-paced, feel-good production that delivers excitement, laughs, and impressive stage spectacle.

reviews.title: Excellent performance of Oliver
reviews.body: I really enjoyed today’s performance of Oliver! in London. It was excellent – the music, lighting, and overall production were fantastic, and the actors all gave very strong performances. I especially loved Fagin, Nancy, and the Artful Dodger, though the entire cast was very good. I was slightly confused by the change in the sequence of events compared to the original, but overall it worked quite well. There were a few moments that felt a bit cheeky, with some unnecessary sexy content, particularly involving Mr Blundell and the “Scream” song, which I didn’t feel added much to the show. That said, it was still a really enjoyable performance. The energy, talent, and atmosphere were great, and I would happily go and see it again. A very entertaining and well-performed production we also couldn’t see all of the performance when they were on the platform or coming down the steps or ladders due to the way we were seated and nobody said anything about restricted for you. I’ll definitely get a ticket on the next floor next time.

reviews.title: Clever Re-staging of Alan Ayckbourn's 1985 Play
reviews.body: Entertaining, well-acted re-staging of Ayckbourn's 1985 play about a woman slipping into a parallel world mentally. We can see that her 'real family' are dull & unappreciative, her husband one of those men who is very wrapped up in himself, while her son has run off to join a strange cult. The play is cleverly staged especially when the 'real' & 'imagined' families interact. It displays the typical Ayckbournian mild mockery of the English middle-classes, but it isn't really a satire. By modern standards, the play is quite slow & there is too much padding to be ideal for current audiences, but it remains amusing and intriguing. Ayckbourn is certainly a master of theatrical dialogue. The acting is very competent; Sheridan Smith plays the main role with energy and conviction, while the supporting cast are better than competent, especially her imaginary husband who has good stage presence & clear diction.

For the best overall view, I’d recommend front middle circle. It’s a bit raunchy in terms of some of the costumes, so bare that in mind for younger kids if planning a family trip. For those very familiar with Luhrmann’s film, since then he negotiated rights to a plethora of songs so expect to hear many familiar including ‘Come What May’ the showstopper however also many new additions. reviews.title: Thank you! You didn’t disappoint
reviews.body: We came to watch Matilda for my daughter’s 6th birthday. She has seen the original movie, and I’ve read her the book it’s one of her absolute favourites. Right from the start, we were surprised with an unexpected and very welcome upgrade. We were seated quickly, and with a 14-year-old brother in tow, we weren’t sure how he’d enjoy it. But searching for the hidden words in the stage display became a fun activity for all of us. The show itself was spectacular. The songs, the acting, and every performance were sensational. My daughter was completely enthralled and couldn’t wait for Miss Trunchbull to appear and she was not disappointed! She left inspired and in awe of Matilda. The storyline flowed beautifully, and the backdrops and transitions were not only seamless but wonderfully entertaining. On the way home, my 14-year-old told us it was one of his best days of 2025 not just because he enjoyed the show, but because he loved seeing his sister so happy. We even bought a “Little Bit Naughty” T-shirt because… sometimes you do have to be a little bit naughty. Thank you for an unforgettable experience.

reviews.title: "Surprised by love"

She had the audience as well as Lewis, eating out of her hand. Great supporting characters too. A beautiful and thought-provoking show..do we need the experience of pain and loss to understand Love? I believe it's the experience of being loved that can help us bear pain and suffering, that gives us belief there is more good in the world than bad and more demonstration of love and valuing of others in life might well lead to less pain and suffering.

reviews.title: Exceptional theatre experience
reviews.body: I wasn’t familiar with the story of All my sons and I’m glad I didn’t look up the text before. Getting to discover the story through this incredible production was such a gift. As an avid theatre goer, intense family dramas on stage can sometimes feel a little drawn out, tiring even. But this play and it’s production truly had me entranced from beginning to end. The production design was effective in its simplicity, there was just enough visual contrast to create depth. I marvelled at the beauty of seeing the actors sat on the tree at different levels, giving beautiful visual symmetry. As for the lighting, I could tell every single adjustment had a dramaturgical objective and it worked really well. I also particularly liked how the use of coloured lights played with our perception of the costumes colours and textures. The costumes were modern, clothes that would be considered casually fashionable for 2026. It gave me a visual sense of familiarity. I particularly enjoyed how the colours of every character’s outfits complemented each other, once again creating a visual balance. As for the acting, all I can say is that it was so good, I was completely emotionally invested in the story, in finding out everything that the play would allow me to know about these characters and their lives.

After the performance my wife and I both agreed that the performance far exceeded any hopes or expectations we had. Every performer was uniquely brilliant; their voices and character work were spot on. The musicians were immaculate and the lighting did an amazing job at following the energetic performers. For a show that spent the whole time in view of the audience, the whole ensemble maintained a high level of energy and maintained the attention and interest of the audience from beginning to the end. My wife was delighted. I went from being passive in my excitement to a fully fledged fan of the show. A wonderful experience and performance. Well done all!

reviews.title: Amazing my first theatre show
reviews.body: Wicked" isn't just a musical; it's an utterly exhilarating journey that left me utterly spellbound from start to finish. From the moment the curtain rose, I found myself swept away, laughing joyfully one minute and shedding heartfelt tears the next. The sheer power and beauty of the voices on stage gave me goosebumps countless times, a testament to the incredible talent resonating through the theatre. This wasn't just a night out; it was a landmark occasion, marking our very first theatre experience for myself and my two sons. To witness their pure delight and excitement was truly special – they absolutely adored every moment, a sentiment I wholeheartedly share. In fact, Wicked is so profoundly captivating, I would happily return to Oz again and again without a moment's hesitation. The young actors delivered performances showcasing an astonishing depth of talent. Their powerful voices and flawless singing were nothing short of breathtaking, perfectly complemented by the utterly spectacular costumes that brought the vibrant world of Oz to life. Every element, from the vibrant visuals to the soaring music, was magnificent, making "Wicked" an unforgettable spectacle that perfectly blends magic, emotion, and unparalleled artistry. Truly amazing!

reviews.title: Totally worth every penny – highly recommend!
reviews.body: This stage play perfectly captures the Stranger Things vibe and tells a thrilling, heartbreaking origin story for Vecna (young Henry Creel). His loneliness, inner struggle, and fall into darkness made me feel both terrified and a little sympathetic toward the villain. The nearly three-hour show flies by with tight pacing, blending funny high-school moments with intense horror. The special effects are pure magic: people levitating, illusions switching in seconds, and the Upside Down invading the stage – I jumped several times and couldn’t look away. The cast is outstanding, especially Louis McCartney as Henry, who nails the creepy inner torment. For any Stranger Things fan, this is a must-see that fills in so many gaps from the series. Even if you haven’t watched the show, it’s still an incredible visual and emotional ride. Totally worth every penny – highly recommend!

reviews.title: Chill wind across the Wall
reviews.body: A film of a book by LeCarre, Richard Burton and Claire Bloom, stark b/w fiilming and memorable theme tune, so a lot to live up to. From the opening scenes on stage it became apparent that we were in for something special, and that performing 'in the round' had been addressed very imaginatively. The ghostly appearance of George Smiley grounded us into the world of The Circus and the spectacled world from Alec Guiness.There was a scene in the production of Alec Lemas being tortured by water, and this was genuinely scary. It was hard not to hold breath whilst it was going on, and getting real concern for actor Rory Keenan. I think it would not be suitable for impressionable children. Perhaps the role of Munt should have been played by a more hunky actor, as menace was missing, and the diction of the man in the labour exchange could have been a tad better, but overall this was an absolutely superb evenings entertainment. As far as the theatre itsself, the view from the first balcony was first class, as was the acoustics. An extra six inches of leg room would have been welcome. Unfortunately toileting provision was the worst I have encountered, with men queing up outside. The signage was Woke over practicality causing a lot of confusion. Exiting the stairway was a real chocking point and I wonder how planning was given. All told though, like anywhere, further visits will reveal tricks to avoid the pitfalls and my experience of The Spy Who Came In From The Cold was Great!

reviews.title: Excellent re-imagining of a classic
reviews.body: This show is packed with excellence. Uniformly strong performances and a thoughtful, tense script that makes the most of resonances with current-day American politics have turned a great movie into a terrific piece of theatre. The ever-present station clock stands centrally, high above the action, beating down on the stage like the noon sun and inexorably ticking down in (almost) real time to the moment of Kane's seismic confrontation with Miller, while superb lighting and stage effects join in to create the suffocatingly dry dusty heat of New Mexico. This is a parable about the cost of doing the right thing, and without giving any spoilers, it sidesteps the all-too-neatly packaged ending of the 1952 movie and replaces it with an ambivalent denouement that is a million miles away from neat. Some of the choices of music were a little odd, anachronistic, or even jarring, but did not detract from the whole show. My only advice would be to go and see this now.

We were blown away by the acting, the singing, the staging, the beautiful costumes, and the incredible props. Everything on stage was world-class, and we enjoyed it immensely. During the interval we saw a mouse run across the floor. It genuinely startled us and, for me, it made it difficult to stay fully focused on the second half of the show. Even with these issues, it was still a memorable night that we’ll remember for a long time. Given the partially blocked view from my friend’s seat and the presence of a mouse during the interval, we feel part of the experience was compromised. We would appreciate a partial refund or appropriate compensation for these issues, much appreciated.

Some of the singing was a bit off key but i could live with it as the rest of the show was spectacular. I could definitely have done without the child performer. Her voice was hard on the ears and just in general I didn't enjoy her. I am sure her part in the storyline was necessary however with the overall magic - the amazing lighting and staging, there must be some other way to get around having her there. No matter where you sit in the theatre you have a comfortable seat. This is my 2nd visit and both times I sat in the Locomotive section which I believe gives the best view of the whole performance.

reviews.body: We first saw Arcadia when it was performed at The National under Trevor Nunn, with Rufus Sewell, Felicity Kendall and Bill Nighy. Although the production in the round worked well and the audience loved it (and I can see that this setting provides almost twice the number of seats), I very much missed the gorgeous earlier set with the beautiful room and the sunlit parkland back-drop seen through the huge wrought iron windows. Also the physical doors either side of the stage, banging and slamming, were missed. I did also wonder if the cast was a bit miscast. The actors all seemed to be the same age, which lost the variation of the the youth of the 19th century Thomasina and Septimus compared to the older modern-day Hannah and Bernard. But it was a great evening and we thoroughly enjoyed the production.

Some of the innuendoes I missed (as did quite a few in the audience which was observed and commented on by those on stage!...with humour of course). Good audience interactions from the stage in what is a very people-centric theatre with performers entering and leaving the stage through the audience. I would recommend the visitor understands the underlying structure of the story and messaging to optimise what they get from the scripting and delivery. But absolutely excellent - all of them - and highly recommended.

reviews.title: Wonderful acting but Sorkin is a little too preachy
reviews.body: The acting, set design and costumes were outstanding. I loved the self-referential narrative by the three kids who were wonderfully engaging. I didn't enjoy Aaron Sorkin’s revisions of the script that hit the audience over the head with the moral. The novel does it so much better. Calpurnia’s criticisms of Atticus were incredibly jarring as was Bob Ewell’s intellectual comments about race and America generally. You can't put 2022 sensibility into 1930s characters’ mouths.
reviews.author: Elaine

reviews.title: Beautiful enhancement of the original book

I appreciated the multifaceted black characters (they were more active than in Harper Lee’s book, as I remember it) and the total relevance to today’s race relations and gender expectations. Very moving, as I’d expect from Aaron Sorkin, because it’s so well-acted and it’s creatively done — but not so creative that the time it’s set in can be forgotten.
reviews.author: Jennifer

reviews.body: I haven’t been to a play for decades (my bad) - usually musicals. I left this production stunned. It was magnificent, absolutely magnificent. It made me think ‘if you want to see proper acting’ this is it’. Stunning performances. And I should have known it would be a good production if Mr Sorkin was involved but it blew me away. Breathtakingly brilliant. And the sets! Wow! Genius, absolute genius. An experience I’ll never forget. Thank you all so much, congratulations to everyone involved.

reviews.title: Dissapointment
reviews.body: The seats in this theater are very unkomfortable and the leg space is next to nothing. Even just because of that, it is quite hard to try to enjoy any kind of entertainment. The show itself was a bit of a dissapointment, I expected more, and my feeling was the show was a bit outdated. The music was not performed live, just the vocals. The playback of the music was in an 80's style synth and fake string arrangements, that were not impressing. On top of that the mix of the playback to the vocals was not done well and did not always blend well together. Also the vocals were dry and did not seem to have any kind of reverb on it at times. As a resault the music was not so impressive. But once I did have massive goosebumps because of a fantastic performance. And that was the song Memories performed by Bevegley Knight. A fantastic performance, and by far the best of them all. Because of this wonderful performance I stayed the whole time, waiting for another moment like that.

reviews.body: Show was absolutely fantastic. Acting, singing, the set - everything was brilliant! We loved it SO much. Very minor and boring points but worth mentioning as we commented at the time - it would be great to have more seats in the bar area as you can’t go to your seats straight away so would be able to sit down. They were all reserved . Also, it would be great if there were more toilets - we couldn’t use the loo in the break as the line was too long as the interval was (understandably) 20 mins.

reviews.title: Once-in-a-lifetime experience
reviews.body: The show itself was absolutely fantastic — truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience for both of us. We were blown away by the acting, the singing, the staging, the beautiful costumes, and the incredible props. Everything on stage was world-class, and we enjoyed it immensely. During the interval we saw a mouse run across the floor. It genuinely startled us and, for me, it made it difficult to stay fully focused on the second half of the show. Even with these issues, it was still a memorable night that we’ll remember for a long time. Given the partially blocked view from my friend’s seat and the presence of a mouse during the interval, we feel part of the experience was compromised. We would appreciate a partial refund or appropriate compensation for these issues, much appreciated.

reviews.title: Immersive Spectacluar
reviews.body: These are probably the most expensive theatre tickets I'll ever purchase (£360 each for stage-side seats), but it was for the love of my life on Valentine's Day so I justified it as birthday, Christmas and Valentine's Day present. Anyway I had heard it's best to get there 45-60 mins early to take in the ambiance, see and hear the prologue company, and generally acclimatise yourself to 1930s Berlin. If you're lucky the phone on your table will ring and you can chat to Frauline Kost! The show itself is brilliantly performed with immersive touches, such as the cast interacting with the audience. Casting was superb, with Billy Porter and Marisha Wallace outstanding. Special mention to Alexandra Regan and Lucy Porter who I found out after the show were understudies. You would never have guessed as they were exceptional. There may have been others but the cast was so good you'd never know. Is it worth it? Only your bank balance can tell you that. Is it unforgettable? Absolutely! If you see it (and I recommend you do), make an effort and dress for the occasion. If you don't, you'll stand out as the one who didn't make the effort. This isn't just theatre; this is an immersive spectacular experience...and you're part of the show!

reviews.body:
This was a stunning production, a real privilage to have witnessed. As a lad of fourteen in 1953, I saw Mai Zetterling in the role of Nora at the Lyric Hammersmith and became a devoted fan. However, Hattie Morohan's portrayal last night was simply spell binding, a master class. However, it would be remiss of me to not heap equal praise on the whole cast and production team who made our journey down from the Cotswolds so rewarding and memorable. My wife and I cannot thank you all enough. We wish you every success in all your future endeavours,
Sincerely, Victor S Bennie

reviews.title: Amazing actors but didn't enjoy the interpretation
reviews.body: The actors were amazing, but i didn't enjoy the interpretation of the play. My 16-yr old daughter was upset by how much the play was different f4om the original. But the performance reminded me and made me think about the value of human lives, feelings and unnecessary life demands and traditions that we are expected to satisfy at the high cost to ourselves.
